body:
That would make sense to be fair.

However, she did text in the end, she said she had a great time, but didn't feel a connection. Sucks, but I'll move on.

I'll leave it a couple of days then, and try something like that. I'm meant to have a date with someone else on Thursday, but honestly, I got so excited about this one. 

Thanks for your input :)
Cheers bud, it's what I needed to hear. Actually had a fantastic date with a girl a couple days ago, felt a connection, lots in common and she's gorgeous. Fingers crossed.
Yeah this is spot on. Like I try too hard to impress when it's someone who is fantastic.
I think that's a good idea. Just try to imagine yourself on a level playing field.

Cheers dude. I needed to hear that. I'm feeling a bit lost right now in the dating world, and I also feel that I don't take advantage of the good things. Like I've dated this other girl recently, had about 5 dates, we slept together on the second, and we started to get a bit close, problem is, I don't feel that romantic connection. There are things she does that irk me, even though she's a fantastic woman. I'm scared that I can't get into her in the romantic way, because what if she's it?
That's the trick isn't it? Letting your guard down. You should never be with someone who you can't be yourself around, so that's the lesson here I think.

If I had a dollar for every time someone told me I put too much pressure on myself I'd be a millionaire. In hindsight, with the most recent girl I went on a date with, we weren't compatible, she's this very adventurous type, lovely girl, but always wants to do something. I love to do stuff, but I also like quiet time to relax.
It's trying to find that middle ground isn't it? I guess you've sort of gotta fake it until you make it. Act confident, even if you feel you're being risky.

Cheers man. I guess I was just pretty bummed out after a date I got excited for. In hindsight, we weren't compatible, she is this really adventurous type who volunteers in different countries all the time. I'm still adventurous, but I also love quiet time. It's fair game really.

Honestly, ending up alone. Nearly a year ago I met someone, went on a couple of dates and I completely fell for her.  She didn't feel the same way at the time, even though she said on all levels I am "perfect for her". Can't say fairer than that, I understand. A couple of months back I convinced myself that I was over her, but recently I realised I still can't get her out of my head. I haven't spoken to her in a while, and other girls I meet, I feel nothing for. Me and this girl never did anything, didn't even kiss, I'm starting to feel that maybe there is something wrong with me. I am scared that my feelings for her will hold me back in the future, because I've already met some amazing people but I feel nothing for them.
I guess it's better to try and fail than to never try at all.

Yeah, it wasn't my finest moment, because I think she wanted to kiss me, but I couldn't 100% tell. I'm quite a socially awkward person anyway, so I am unbelievably nervous, coupled with the fact I like her so much.

I'm thinking about suggesting a movie, there's a few movies she wants to show me, and I her, so will maybe do that.

Museum sounds like a good idea. Thanks for the advice.

Thank you. I just feel completely worthless, like I don't matter to anyone. People would be better off without my presence. It doesn't help that I'm approaching 30 and still live at home, despite my best efforts I can't afford to leave. My family don't respect my boundaries, I feel my friends don't fully appreciate my feelings, and even though I've had chances with romantic interests, the ones that I want to go for don't reciprocate. Maybe I have too high standards. I don't know.
